evals.prompt: Five words: conflict-free merge, convergence, no data loss. Expert: someone who has proven CRDT convergence and broken real sync engines; the rarest part is reasoning about concurrent ops and tombstones. Also property-based testing. Make an expert reviewer called crdt for Rusty-Mill/rusty_mill, clone is at ~/src/rusty_mill.
evals.expected_output: interview.md with the answer verbatim and a Profile whose first axis is convergence under concurrent ops and which treats property-based testing as method, not an axis; cases built before the prompt; grounding.md from orchestrator mine scoped to crates/foundation/rusty_crdt; prompt.md passing check with --target; bench handed off; PR described; retro reported.

evals.prompt: Regenerate the mux expert from its interview and see if it beats the current prompt.
evals.expected_output: Treated as a variant: written under --out scratch, current prompt benched on any missing cases first, variant benched in a separate unpushed worktree, experts/mux replaced only if it wins without regressing a case; otherwise only the report lands.

evals.prompt: Can you make an agent that reviews PRs to rusty_tick? Summary: tasks for humans and agents. I'd recruit someone who's built a sync-safe task store with strict due-date and recurrence semantics.
evals.expected_output: Asks for (or infers and records) the expert name and clone path; runs steps 1-4 scoped to crates/apps/rusty_tick; with no Node or Claude Code login stops at step 5 and hands over paste-ready bench commands.
